---
name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
  named obligation open.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

   180	This is the étale counterpart of
   181	`Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyReduced_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange`, and it
   182	discharges the *statement* of `Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced` from a hypothesis about
   183	one scheme, with no quantifier over field extensions.
   184	
   185	The route, and why it needs this project's own converse: mathlib's
   186	`smooth_of_grpObj` wants the full `GeometricallyReduced` class, and
   187	`GeometricallyReduced` has no `MorphismProperty.DescendsAlong` instance at v4.31, so
   188	the general-to-`k̄` reduction is not available from mathlib. What *is* available is
   189	`smooth_of_grpObj_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange` (this project, taking
   190	reducedness over `k̄` alone) composed with this project's
   191	`Smooth.geometricallyReduced` — which is why the single-scheme form is legitimate
   192	here even though it is not derivable in mathlib alone. Both of `Pic0Et`'s inputs to
   193	that engine are unconditional (`locallyOfFiniteType`, `grpObj`). -/
   194	theorem geometricallyReduced_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange
   195	    (h : IsReduced (Limits.pullback (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom
   196	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k)))))) :
   197	    GeometricallyReduced (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := by
   198	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := locallyOfFiniteType C
   199	  letI : GrpObj (Over.mk (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom) := (grpObj C).some
   200	  haveI : Smooth (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
   201	    smooth_of_grpObj_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange _ h
   202	  infer_instance
   203	
   204	/-- **Smoothness of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` from the same single-scheme hypothesis.** The
   205	assembly `Pic0Et.smooth_of_geometricallyReduced` fed by the reduction above. -/
   206	theorem smooth_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange
   207	    (h : IsReduced (Limits.pullback (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom
   208	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k)))))) :
   209	    Smooth (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
   210	  smooth_of_geometricallyReduced C
   211	    (geometricallyReduced_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange C h)
   212	
   213	/-- **The converse: the reduction above loses nothing.** `GeometricallyReduced` of
   214	the structure morphism gives back reducedness of the `k̄` base change, since the base
   215	change of a geometrically reduced morphism along any morphism is geometrically
   216	reduced and `Spec k̄` is reduced.
   217	
   218	Stated because a reduction that is not an equivalence has moved the obstruction
   219	rather than isolated it. Here nothing moved. -/
   220	theorem isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange_of_geometricallyReduced
   221	    (h : GeometricallyReduced (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom) :
   222	    IsReduced (Limits.pullback (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom
   223	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))) := by
   224	  haveI := h
   225	  infer_instance
   226	
   227	/-- **The smoothness obligation of the headline is exactly one single-scheme
   228	statement.** `Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced` holds iff `Pic⁰ ×_{Spec k} Spec k̄` is
   229	reduced.
   230	
   231	Neither side is proved here: this is the equivalence, and the mathematics owed is
   232	Kleiman §5 `cor:sm` (on a curve `H²(C, 𝒪_C) = 0` makes the deformation functor of an
   233	invertible sheaf unobstructed; characteristic-free *because* `dim C = 1`). -/
   234	theorem geometricallyReduced_iff_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange :
   235	    GeometricallyReduced (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom ↔
   236	      IsReduced (Limits.pullback (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom
   237	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))) :=
   238	  ⟨isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange_of_geometricallyReduced C,
   239	    geometricallyReduced_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange C⟩
   240	
   241	/-! ### Properness: the valuative route and the `k̄` route, both transferred -/
   242	
   243	/-- **Universal closedness of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` from the valuative criterion** — the
   244	transfer the board recorded as unmeasured.
   245	
   246	`UniversallyClosed.of_valuativeCriterion` (Stacks 01KF) needs `[QuasiCompact]` of the
   247	morphism, which is `quasiCompact` above, plus `ValuativeCriterion.Existence`, the
   248	hypothesis. So universal closedness on this tower needs no quasi-projectivity
   249	vocabulary — which matters, because mathlib v4.31 has none, and that absence is the
   250	standing reason (`I-0074` Caveat 2) Kleiman's §5 `th:qpp&p` route cannot be
   251	formalised as written.
   252	
   253	Through representability a `Spec R`-point of `Pic⁰` is a relative Picard class, so
   254	the lifting statement is the concrete assertion that an invertible sheaf on
   255	`C ×_k Spec K` extends over the valuation ring — the classical content of properness. -/
   256	theorem universallyClosed_of_valuativeCriterion
   257	    (h : ValuativeCriterion.Existence (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom) :
   258	    UniversallyClosed (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := by
   259	  haveI : QuasiCompact (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := quasiCompact C
   260	  exact UniversallyClosed.of_valuativeCriterion _ h
   261	
   262	/-- **Properness of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` from the valuative existence criterion alone.**
   263	
   264	Every other conjunct of `IsProper` is a theorem: `IsSeparated` is
   265	`Pic0Et.isSeparated` (clopen immersion into the separated ambient `PicSchemeEt`),
   266	`LocallyOfFiniteType` is `Pic0Et.locallyOfFiniteType`, and `QuasiCompact` is
   267	`quasiCompact` above. So this is the sharpest properness reduction available on the
   268	étale tower, and its hypothesis is the only one mathlib has vocabulary for.
   269	
   270	Note that the *ambient* route is refuted and must not be retried: universal
   271	closedness of `Pic_{C/k}` is false, since it would force `CompactSpace` on an
   272	infinite disjoint union over `deg ∈ ℤ` (`Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean`). That does
   273	not touch this statement — `Pic⁰` is quasi-compact, `Pic` is not, and `quasiCompact`
   274	above is precisely the difference. -/
   275	theorem proper_of_valuativeCriterion
   276	    (h : ValuativeCriterion.Existence (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom) :
   277	    IsProper (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := by
   278	  haveI : IsSeparated (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := isSeparated C
   279	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := locallyOfFiniteType C
   280	  haveI := universallyClosed_of_valuativeCriterion C h
   281	  constructor
   282	
   283	/-- **Universal closedness descends from `k̄`** (Stacks 02KS, EGA IV₂ 2.6.4).
   284	
   285	`Spec.map (algebraMap k k̄)` is surjective, flat and quasi-compact, and mathlib
   286	packages the fpqc descent of `UniversallyClosed` along exactly that property as an
   287	instance, so this is one application of
   288	`MorphismProperty.of_pullback_snd_of_descendsAlong`.
   289	
   290	This is the second, independent route to the properness obligation: either lift
   291	valuations (`universallyClosed_of_valuativeCriterion`) or prove closedness over the
   292	algebraic closure. -/
   293	theorem universallyClosed_of_baseChange
   294	    (h : UniversallyClosed (Limits.pullback.snd (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom
   295	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k)))))) :
   296	    UniversallyClosed (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
   297	  MorphismProperty.of_pullback_snd_of_descendsAlong
   298	    (Q := @Surjective ⊓ @Flat ⊓ @QuasiCompact)
   299	    ⟨⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩, inferInstance⟩ h
   300	
   301	/-- **The converse: the `k̄` descent is lossless too.** `UniversallyClosed` is stable
   302	under base change, so the reduction is an equivalence. -/
   303	theorem universallyClosed_baseChange_of_universallyClosed
   304	    (h : UniversallyClosed (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom) :
   305	    UniversallyClosed (Limits.pullback.snd (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom
   306	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))) := by
   307	  haveI := h
   308	  infer_instance
   309	
   310	/-- **The properness obligation of the headline is exactly universal closedness over
   311	`k̄`.** Neither side is proved; this records that the descent isolates the obligation
   312	rather than relocating it. -/
   313	theorem universallyClosed_iff_baseChange :
   314	    UniversallyClosed (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom ↔
   315	      UniversallyClosed (Limits.pullback.snd (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom
   316	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))) :=
   317	  ⟨universallyClosed_baseChange_of_universallyClosed C,
   318	    universallyClosed_of_baseChange C⟩
   319	
   320	/-- **Properness of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` from universal closedness over `k̄` alone.**
   321	
   322	Assembled conjunct-by-conjunct rather than by descending `IsProper` itself, because
   323	**`IsProper` does not fpqc-descend at mathlib v4.31**: `DescendsAlong @IsProper
   324	(@Surjective ⊓ @Flat ⊓ @QuasiCompact)` fails to synthesize, while the same statement
   325	for `@UniversallyClosed` is an instance. Measured, and recorded here so the shorter
   326	proof is not attempted again. -/
   327	theorem proper_of_baseChange
   328	    (h : UniversallyClosed (Limits.pullback.snd (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom
   329	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k)))))) :
   330	    IsProper (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := by
   331	  haveI : IsSeparated (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := isSeparated C
   332	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := locallyOfFiniteType C
   333	  haveI := universallyClosed_of_baseChange C h
   334	  constructor
   335	
   336	/-! ### The abelian-variety package, on the tower the headline uses -/
   337	
   338	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is an abelian variety, from two single-scheme inputs over `k̄`.**
   339	
   340	The étale counterpart of `Scheme.Pic0.isAbelianVariety`, which is stated under
   341	`[HasPicScheme C]` — a class with no instance, hence about no curve. This version is
   342	stated on `Pic0SchemeEt C`, the object `picardJacobianWitness` uses.
   343	
   344	Two of the four conjuncts (`GeometricallyIrreducible`, `Nonempty (GrpObj …)`) are
   345	unconditional theorems of `Pic0Et.lean`. The other two are supplied by the two
   346	hypotheses, which are exactly the residues isolated above:
   347	
   348	* `hred : IsReduced (Pic⁰ ×_{Spec k} Spec k̄)` — Kleiman §5 `cor:sm`;
   349	* `huc : UniversallyClosed (Pic⁰ ×_{Spec k} Spec k̄)` — Kleiman §5 `th:qpp&p`.
   350	
   351	Both are **hypotheses**: this is the assembly, not a discharge, and no curve is
   352	exhibited for which either holds. -/
   353	theorem isAbelianVariety_of_baseChange
   354	    (hred : IsReduced (Limits.pullback (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom
   355	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))))
   356	    (huc : UniversallyClosed (Limits.pullback.snd (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom
   357	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k)))))) :
   358	    IsProper (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom ∧ Smooth (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom ∧
   359	      GeometricallyIrreducible (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom ∧
   360	      Nonempty (GrpObj (Pic0SchemeEt C)) :=
   361	  ⟨proper_of_baseChange C huc, smooth_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange C hred,
   362	    geometricallyIrreducible C, grpObj C⟩
   363	
   364	/-- **The same package from the valuative form of properness.** Identical except that
   365	closedness comes from lifting valuations rather than from `k̄`; kept because the two
   366	properness hypotheses are not interderivable by anything in this file. -/
   367	theorem isAbelianVariety_of_valuativeCriterion
   368	    (hred : IsReduced (Limits.pullback (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom
   369	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))))
   370	    (hvc : ValuativeCriterion.Existence (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom) :
   371	    IsProper (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom ∧ Smooth (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom ∧
   372	      GeometricallyIrreducible (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom ∧
   373	      Nonempty (GrpObj (Pic0SchemeEt C)) :=
   374	  ⟨proper_of_valuativeCriterion C hvc,
   375	    smooth_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange C hred,
   376	    geometricallyIrreducible C, grpObj C⟩

     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# `Pic⁰_{C/k}` over an arbitrary base field
    12	
    13	The identity component of the Picard scheme representing the **étale-sheafified**
    14	relative Picard functor — the Jacobian candidate of the headline, available for
    15	every smooth proper geometrically integral curve with **no hypothesis on
    16	`C(k)`** (owner decision of 2026-07-28, protection I-0491).
    17	
    18	## Why this file exists beside `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`
    19	
    20	That file develops `Pic⁰` for `Scheme.Pic0Scheme C = IdentityComponent
    21	(PicScheme C)`, the identity component of the scheme representing the
    22	*unsheafified* functor `picSharp C`. Since the owner decision, the sole producer
    23	of that scheme's existence gate is the conditional
    24	`Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`, so everything there is a statement about a
    25	**pointed** curve. Its mathematics is not wasted — the tangent-space chain and
    26	the dimension count are exactly the same arguments — but the *object* the
    27	headline needs is the identity component of `PicSchemeEt C`.
    28	
    29	Two of the four abelian-variety properties come for free at this level, and two
    30	do not, which is the same split as in the `picSharp` development:
    31	
    32	* `Pic0Et.grpObj` and `Pic0Et.geometricallyIrreducible` are **proved** here, from
    33	  the unconditional `groupSchemeStructureEt` and
    34	  `GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`;
    35	* `Pic0Et.isSeparated` is **proved**, from the unconditional separatedness of
    36	  `PicSchemeEt` along the clopen immersion;
    37	* `Pic0Et.smooth` and `Pic0Et.proper` are the two remaining obligations of the
    38	  headline, and both are stated here as **assemblies** rather than as bare
    39	  `sorry`s, following the run-0067 reduction of the `picSharp` side
    40	  (`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`). Their actual residues are one statement
    41	  each:
    42	  - `Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced` — Cartier's theorem in characteristic zero, a
    43	    genuine statement in characteristic `p`. Everything else in smoothness is
    44	    mathlib's `smooth_of_grpObj` plus the two inputs proved above;
    45	  - `Pic0Et.universallyClosed` — Kleiman §5 Thm. `th:qpp&p`. The other two
    46	    conjuncts of properness (separatedness, local finiteness) are proved.
    47	
    48	  Both residues are **true statements**, in contrast with the deleted
    49	  rational-point leaf, which was false.
    50	
    51	## References
    52	
    53	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §5 (`lem:agps`, `prp:pic0`,
    54	Thm. `thm:tgtsp`). Blueprint: `def:pic_zero_subscheme`,
    55	`thm:pic_zero_is_abelian_variety`.
    56	-/
    57	
    58	set_option autoImplicit false
    59	
    60	universe u
    61	
    62	open CategoryTheory
    63	
    64	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    65	
    66	namespace Scheme
    67	
    68	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` over an arbitrary base field**: the identity component of the
    69	scheme representing the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor.
    70	
    71	Unconditional — no `[HasRationalPoint C]`, and no `[HasPicScheme C]`. The two
    72	inputs `GroupScheme.IdentityComponent` requires are both available for
    73	`PicSchemeEt C` without hypotheses on `C(k)`: the group structure
    74	`groupSchemeStructureEt` (Yoneda transport of the étale sheaf's abelian-group
    75	structure) and `instPicSchemeEtLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman §4 `th:main`(1),
    76	extracted from the representability package).
    77	
    78	This is the Jacobian candidate of the headline. When `genus C = 0` it is
    79	`Spec k`, with no separate construction: the tangent space `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is then
    80	`0`-dimensional. -/
    81	noncomputable def Pic0SchemeEt {k : Type u} [Field k]
    82	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    83	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    84	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
    85	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
    86	  GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicSchemeEt C)
    87	
    88	namespace Pic0Et
    89	
    90	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is a group scheme** — PROVED, unconditionally.
    91	
    92	The identity component of a `k`-group scheme locally of finite type is an open
    93	and closed subgroup scheme (`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme`,
    94	Kleiman §5 Lem. `lem:agps`(3)), and its group structure is the one transported
    95	onto `PicSchemeEt C` from the étale Picard sheaf by
    96	`groupSchemeStructureEt`. Neither step needs a rational point.
    97	
    98	Stated as `Nonempty` because `GrpObj` is data and the identity-component
    99	substrate delivers the subgroup-scheme structure existentially. -/
   100	theorem grpObj {k : Type u} [Field k]
   101	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   102	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   103	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
   104	    Nonempty (GrpObj (Pic0SchemeEt C)) :=
   105	  GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism (PicSchemeEt C)
   106	
   107	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is geometrically irreducible** — PROVED, unconditionally.
   108	
   109	`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible` (Kleiman §5
   110	Lem. `lem:agps`): the identity component of a `k`-group scheme locally of finite
   111	type is locally of finite type, quasi-compact and geometrically irreducible. Only
   112	the third conjunct is taken here. -/
   113	theorem geometricallyIrreducible {k : Type u} [Field k]
   114	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   115	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   116	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
   117	    GeometricallyIrreducible (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
   118	  (GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible
   119	    (PicSchemeEt C)).2.2
   120	
   121	/-- `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is locally of finite type over `k` — PROVED, unconditionally
   122	(first conjunct of `isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`). -/
   123	theorem locallyOfFiniteType {k : Type u} [Field k]
   124	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   125	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   126	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
   127	    LocallyOfFiniteType (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
   128	  (GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible
   129	    (PicSchemeEt C)).1
   130	
   131	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is smooth over `k`** — OPEN OBLIGATION, and a **true**
   132	statement.
   133	
   134	Kleiman §5: a group scheme locally of finite type over a field is smooth as soon
   135	as it is geometrically reduced. Mathlib's `smooth_of_grpObj` takes exactly
   136	`[LocallyOfFiniteType f]`, `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` and `[GeometricallyReduced f]`
   137	over an arbitrary field, and the first two are proved above
   138	(`locallyOfFiniteType`, `grpObj`). So the entire remaining content is
   139	`GeometricallyReduced (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom` — Cartier's theorem in
   140	characteristic zero, and a genuine characteristic-`p` statement otherwise. It
   141	does not synthesize, and its only producer in the tree is
   142	`Smooth.geometricallyReduced`, which would be circular.
   143	
   144	This is the étale-formulation counterpart of `Scheme.Pic0.smooth`, and it is one
   145	of the five obligations of the Jacobian headline. Following the run-0067 reduction
   146	of the `picSharp` side (`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`), it is stated here as an
   147	**assembly** rather than an obligation: the translation argument is mathlib's and
   148	the two other inputs are proved above, so the obligation proper is
   149	`geometricallyReduced` below and nothing else. -/
   150	theorem smooth_of_geometricallyReduced {k : Type u} [Field k]
   151	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   152	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   153	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C]
   154	    (h : GeometricallyReduced (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom) :
   155	    Smooth (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := by
   156	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := locallyOfFiniteType C
   157	  haveI := h
   158	  letI : GrpObj (Over.mk (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom) := (grpObj C).some
   159	  exact smooth_of_grpObj (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom
   160	
   161	/-- **The sole remaining input to smoothness: geometric reducedness of
   162	`Pic⁰_{C/k}`** — OPEN OBLIGATION, a **true** statement.
   163	
   164	Cartier's theorem in characteristic zero; in characteristic `p` a genuine
   165	statement (it is where `H²(C, 𝒪_C) = 0` enters on the `picSharp` side). It does
   166	not synthesize, and its only producer in the tree is
   167	`Smooth.geometricallyReduced`, which would be circular here.
   168	
   169	This is the étale counterpart of `Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyReduced`. -/
   170	theorem geometricallyReduced {k : Type u} [Field k]
   171	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   172	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   173	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
   174	    GeometricallyReduced (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
   175	  sorry
   176	
   177	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is smooth over `k`** — assembly of
   178	`smooth_of_geometricallyReduced` with its single open input. -/
   179	theorem smooth {k : Type u} [Field k]
   180	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   181	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   182	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicSchemeEt C] :
   183	    Smooth (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
   184	  smooth_of_geometricallyReduced C (geometricallyReduced C)
   185	
   186	/-- **`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is proper over `k`** — OPEN OBLIGATION, and a **true**
   187	statement.
   188	
   189	Kleiman §5 Prp. `prp:pic0`: the identity component of the Picard scheme of a
   190	smooth proper curve is proper (indeed projective) over the base. Quasi-compactness
   191	of the identity component is available
   192	(`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`, second
   193	conjunct) and separatedness descends from `instPicSchemeEtIsSeparated` along the
   194	clopen immersion; what is missing is universal closedness, which is where the
   195	properness of `C` enters through the Abel map.
   196	
   197	This is the étale-formulation counterpart of `Scheme.Pic0.proper`, and it is one
   198	of the five obligations of the Jacobian headline. As with smoothness, it is stated
   199	as an **assembly**: two of the three conjuncts of properness are proved, so the
   200	obligation proper is `universallyClosed` below. -/
   201	theorem isSeparated {k : Type u} [Field k]

     6	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Group.Smooth
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Smoothness of a group scheme from reducedness over ONE algebraic closure
    10	
    11	Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_grpObj` proves that a group scheme locally of finite
    12	type over a field is smooth as soon as it is **geometrically** reduced, i.e. as soon as
    13	`X ×_k Spec K` is reduced for *every* field `K` and every `Spec K ⟶ Spec k`. Internally it
    14	goes through a `private` lemma which needs only reducedness of the **single** base change to
    15	the algebraic closure — the geometric content is the translation argument at an algebraically
    16	closed base, and the general field case is obtained by flat descent along `Spec k̄ → Spec k`.
    17	
    18	That `private` modifier is the whole reason for this file. Both this project and the sibling
    19	`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` reached the same conclusion independently (inbox
    20	I-0495, 2026-07-28): the smoothness leg of "`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is an abelian variety" wants to
    21	supply reducedness over `k̄` and nothing more, because
    22	
    23	* `Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced` is *defined* by base change to an algebraic closure
    24	  (`Mathlib/RingTheory/Nilpotent/GeometricallyReduced.lean`), so at the algebra level the
    25	  k̄-statement is the definition rather than a special case;
    26	* the scheme-level class `GeometricallyReduced` quantifies over all field base changes, and
    27	  the passage from the `k̄` case to that quantifier is **absent from mathlib v4.31** — it is
    28	  the transcendental half of `IsReduced after base change to k̄ ⟹ GeometricallyReduced`,
    29	  which has no producer in mathlib and no `MorphismProperty.DescendsAlong` instance either
    30	  (verified by machine on both sides, recorded on inbox I-0495).
    31	
    32	So the honest input to smoothness is the `k̄` one, and the cross-project thread priced getting
    33	it as *an upstream PR making `smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed` public*. It is cheaper than
    34	that: the `private` proof uses only public API, so it can simply be re-derived here. This
    35	file does that and then packages the descent step, giving a smoothness criterion whose
    36	hypothesis is a single `IsReduced`.
    37	
    38	## Main results
    39	
    40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed'` — the re-derivation of mathlib's
    41	  `private` lemma: a reduced group scheme locally of finite type over an algebraically closed
    42	  field is smooth. Proof transcribed from `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Smooth.lean`
    43	  (Andrew Yang), which is why the `set_option`s and the `open`s are the same.
    44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_grpObj_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange` — the
    45	  criterion this project actually consumes: `G ⟶ Spec k` is smooth as soon as the base change
    46	  `G ×_{Spec k} Spec k̄` is reduced. No `GeometricallyReduced`, no quantifier over fields.

/-- **The uniqueness half of the valuative criterion is FREE on this tower.**

`ValuativeCriterion` is `Existence ⊓ Uniqueness` (`ValuativeCriterion.eq`), and
`IsSeparated.valuativeCriterion` supplies the second factor from separatedness — which
is `Pic0Et.isSeparated`, a theorem. So the *whole* criterion reduces to `Existence`,
with no second obligation hiding in the uniqueness clause. -/
theorem valuativeCriterion_uniqueness :
    ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := by
  haveI : IsSeparated (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := isSeparated C
  exact IsSeparated.valuativeCriterion _

/-- **Quasi-separatedness is free too**, from separatedness. The third side condition of
mathlib's `IsProper.of_valuativeCriterion`. -/
theorem quasiSeparated : QuasiSeparated (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := by
  haveI : IsSeparated (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := isSeparated C
  infer_instance

/-- **The full valuative criterion from `Existence` alone.** -/
theorem valuativeCriterion_of_existence
    (h : ValuativeCriterion.Existence (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom) :
    ValuativeCriterion (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
  ValuativeCriterion.iff.mpr ⟨h, valuativeCriterion_uniqueness C⟩

/-- **Properness directly from mathlib's `IsProper.of_valuativeCriterion`** — a second,
independent assembly of properness, and the sharpest statement of the properness
obligation available here.

All three side conditions mathlib asks for are theorems on this tower:
`QuasiCompact` (`quasiCompact`), `QuasiSeparated` (`quasiSeparated`) and
`LocallyOfFiniteType` (`Pic0Et.locallyOfFiniteType`); the `Uniqueness` half of the
criterion is `valuativeCriterion_uniqueness`. So `ValuativeCriterion.Existence` is
**the entire remaining content of properness** for `Pic⁰` on the étale tower — not one
of several missing pieces.

Compare `proper_of_valuativeCriterion` above, which reaches the same conclusion through
`UniversallyClosed`. Both are kept: this one shows the residue is exactly `Existence`,
that one exhibits the `UniversallyClosed` conjunct explicitly for the `k̄` route. -/
theorem proper_of_valuativeCriterion_existence
    (h : ValuativeCriterion.Existence (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom) :
    IsProper (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := by
  haveI : QuasiCompact (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := quasiCompact C
  haveI : QuasiSeparated (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := quasiSeparated C
  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom := locallyOfFiniteType C
  exact IsProper.of_valuativeCriterion _ (valuativeCriterion_of_existence C h)

/-- **A purely topological route to the properness residue.**
`ValuativeCriterion.Existence.of_specializingMap`: universal specialization-lifting of
the underlying continuous map suffices. Recorded because it needs no valuation rings and
no invertible-sheaf extension argument — it is a statement about the topology of
`Pic⁰_{C/k}` — and is therefore a genuinely different attack on the same obligation. -/
theorem valuativeCriterion_existence_of_specializingMap
    (h : (topologically @SpecializingMap).universally (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom) :
    ValuativeCriterion.Existence (Pic0SchemeEt C).hom :=
  ValuativeCriterion.Existence.of_specializingMap _ h

/-- **Universal closedness descends from `k̄`** (Stacks 02KS, EGA IV₂ 2.6.4).
